mainTopic: Who may groom on חול המועד: the reason for the ban, cases of being held back, overseas travelers, and a newborn
overview: This amud finishes the משנה's list of people who may launder on חול המועד. The list includes a released מנודה, someone freed from a vow, certain towels, and people becoming טהור. Everyone else is forbidden. The גמרא explains why: the ban pushes people to groom before the רגל, just as the אנשי משמר may not groom during their week of service so they do not arrive untidy. רבי זירא asks about someone delayed by a lost item. אביי forbids it, because onlookers cannot see his reason, like the סריקין of ביתוס. The one-shirt man is allowed because his belt shows why he is laundering, and in רב אשי's version the craftsman case ends in תיקו. The גמרא then shows that רבי יהודה disagrees with the משנה about a traveler returning from overseas. רבא explains that they argue only about a trip for extra profit, and a ברייתא of רבי is reread to fit his explanation. Finally, שמואל permits a haircut for a baby born on the מועד, and רב פנחס begins a challenge from a ברייתא linking the מועד and mourning, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Last people on the laundering list: one released from נידוי and one released from a vow
steps.stepSummary: The משנה adds two more people to its list of those allowed to launder on חול המועד: a מנודה whose ban was lifted, and someone whose vow was undone by a חכם.
steps.simpleTranslation: Also allowed: a person who was under a ban and the Sages released him, and a person who asked a Sage about his vow and was released from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה is in the middle of its list of people who may launder their clothes on חול המועד. It adds two more cases before moving on to towels.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both people were blocked from laundering before the יום טוב, and the block was lifted only during the festival. A מנודה may not launder, and the vow kept the other person from doing it. Since neither could prepare beforehand, they are allowed now.

keyTerms.meaning: A person placed under a ban (נידוי) by the Sages
Asked a Sage to undo his vow

phrases.english: and one under a ban whom the Sages released,
and likewise one who asked a Sage and was released.
phrases.notes: He had vowed not to launder his clothes, and a חכם undid the vow during the festival.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: A released מנודה and someone released from a vow during the festival may launder their clothes on חול המועד.

steps.title: Towels and people leaving טומאה may be laundered for
steps.stepSummary: The משנה permits laundering certain towels that get dirty quickly. It also permits laundering for זבים, זבות, נדות, יולדות, and anyone becoming טהור during the festival.
steps.simpleTranslation: Hand towels, barbers' towels, and drying towels may be washed. Also זבים, זבות, נדות, women after childbirth, and anyone going from טומאה to טהרה may launder. All of these are permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues its list of what may be laundered on חול המועד. It adds certain towels and people who become טהור during the festival.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The towels get dirty constantly, so washing them before יום טוב would not help. The people become טהור in the middle of the festival and need clean clothes then, so they could not have done it earlier.

keyTerms.meaning: Men or women with a טמא bodily flow
Those going from impurity to purity

phrases.english: Hand towels
and barbers' towels
and body-drying towels,
men with a flow and women with a flow
and menstruating women and women who gave birth,
and all who go up from impurity to purity —
these are permitted.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: Towels that get dirty quickly, and people becoming טהור during the festival, may be laundered for on חול המועד.

steps.title: Everyone else is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The משנה closes with a general rule: anyone not on these lists may not cut hair or launder on חול המועד.
steps.simpleTranslation: But all other people are forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the general rule behind all the lists. The exceptions are allowed, and everyone else is not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This line shows that the lists are exceptions to a broader prohibition. It is the line the גמרא will question next.
steps.whatToRemember: Cutting hair and laundering on חול המועד are generally forbidden. The משנה's lists are exceptions.

phrases.english: But all other people are forbidden.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: Anyone not specifically permitted may not cut hair or launder on חול המועד.

steps.title: Why are ordinary people forbidden?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason that everyone else may not cut hair or launder on חול המועד.
steps.simpleTranslation: And all other people: what is the reason they are forbidden?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by asking for the reason behind the משנה's last line. This sets up the answer that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Looking nice for יום טוב seems like a good thing, so why stop it? The גמרא wants the logic of the prohibition.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion of the משנה

phrases.english: GEMARA
And all other people —
what is the reason they are forbidden?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּשְׁאָר כׇּל אָדָם מַאי טַעְמָא אֲסוּרִין
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason that ordinary people may not cut hair or launder on חול המועד.

steps.title: A parallel from the אנשי משמר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers with a משנה about the כהנים on duty in the מקדש. During their week of service they may not cut hair or launder, except on Thursday in honor of שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned: the men of the משמר and the men of the מעמד may not cut hair or launder. On Thursday they are permitted, in honor of שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by quoting another משנה with a similar rule. This is meant to explain the prohibition on חול המועד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The כהנים on duty are forbidden to groom during their week of service, even though looking nice there would seem fitting. The גמרא brings this as the model for the festival rule. The exact reason behind that rule is spelled out right after this.

keyTerms.meaning: As we learned in a משנה
The כהנים whose week it is to serve in the מקדש
Representatives of ישראל who accompanied the service
To cut hair and to launder

phrases.english: As we learned in a mishna:
phrases.notes: This משנה is in תענית, דף טו עמוד ב.

phrases.english: The men of the priestly watch and the men of the non-priestly watch
are forbidden to cut hair and to launder,
but on Thursday they are permitted
because of the honor of Shabbat.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּדִתְנַן: אַנְשֵׁי מִשְׁמָר וְאַנְשֵׁי מַעֲמָד אֲסוּרִין לְסַפֵּר וּלְכַבֵּס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 4 by bringing a parallel rule.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The prohibition on חול המועד follows the same pattern as the rule for the אנשי משמר, who may not cut hair or launder during their week of service.
steps.confusionAlert: The quoted rule is about the week a כהן serves in the מקדש, not about יום טוב. The גמרא brings it only as a parallel to explain the festival rule.

steps.title: The reason: so people do not arrive untidy
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר בר חנה in the name of רבי אלעזר explains the reason behind the משמר rule. The כהנים may not groom during their week so they will not enter their משמר untidy. The same reason applies to the רגל.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי אלעזר: What is the reason? So that they do not enter their watch while untidy. Here too, the rule is so that people do not enter the festival while untidy.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the answer it started in Step 5. It gives the reason behind the משמר rule and applies that same reason to חול המועד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the כהנים could get a haircut in the middle of their week, they would put it off and start their service looking messy. Banning it forces them to groom beforehand. In the same way, banning haircuts and laundry on חול המועד pushes everyone to get ready before the רגל begins.

keyTerms.meaning: Their watch, the week the group of כהנים serves in the מקדש
Here too, applying the same logic

steps.whatToRemember: Grooming is banned on חול המועד so that people get it done before the רגל and do not enter the festival looking messy.
steps.whyThisMatters: This reason is what makes the exceptions in the משנה make sense. The people on that list had no chance to groom before the רגל, so the reason for the ban does not apply to them.

phrases.english: And Rabba bar bar Ḥana said
that Rabbi Elazar said:
What is the reason?
So that they do not enter their watch
while they are untidy.
Here too:
so that they do not enter the festival
while they are untidy.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer from Step 5 by explaining its reason and applying it to the רגל.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ban exists so that people groom before the רגל and do not enter it untidy, just like the כהנים before their משמר.

steps.title: What about someone delayed by a lost item?
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא asks about a person who lost something on ערב הרגל and was too busy to groom. Since he was held back by forces beyond his control, may he groom on חול המועד? Or is it forbidden because onlookers cannot tell why he is doing it?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא asked: If someone lost an item on the eve of the festival, is he permitted because he was forced? Or perhaps, since the reason is not obvious to others, is he not permitted?
steps.whatsHappening: Using the reason just given, רבי זירא asks a new question about a person who was unable to get ready before the רגל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On one side, he did not put off his grooming on purpose, so the reason for the ban does not fit him. On the other side, the people on the משנה's list have a visible reason, while nobody can see that he was busy searching for a lost item.

keyTerms.meaning: Forced by circumstances beyond his control
The matter is not obvious to onlookers

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira asked:
If he lost an item on the eve of the festival,
since he was forced, is he permitted?

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִלְמָא כֵּיוָן דְּלָא מוֹכְחָא מִילְּתָא — לָא?
phrases.english: Or perhaps, since the matter is not obvious, he is not?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the reason from Step 6 to a new case that the משנה does not list.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does being forced by circumstances permit grooming on חול המועד even when onlookers cannot see the reason?

steps.title: אביי: people will see an unfair exception
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that it is forbidden. He compares it to the case of the סריקין cakes, where חכמים did not allow ביתוס an exception because people would say, 'All the סריקין are forbidden, but ביתוס's are allowed?!'
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: People would say, 'All the סריקין are forbidden, yet the סריקין of ביתוס are permitted?!'
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers רבי זירא's question with a well-known line, showing that חכמים do not allow exceptions that onlookers cannot understand.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the סריקין case, ביתוס may have had a good reason to be allowed, but people looking on would only see one person breaking the rule everyone else keeps. In the same way, the man who lost an item looks like anyone else grooming on חול המועד, so he is not permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: Decorated cakes, which חכמים forbade baking for פסח
ביתוס, a man who wanted an exception to make these cakes

phrases.english: Abaye said: People will say:
All the decorated cakes are forbidden,
phrases.notes: He is quoting a known line about cakes חכמים banned for פסח. They refused ביתוס an exception even though his reason was good.

phrases.english: but the decorated cakes of Baitos are permitted?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי יֹאמְרוּ כׇּל הַסְּרִיקִין אֲסוּרִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי זירא's question with the second option: it is forbidden.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It is forbidden, because an exception that onlookers cannot see looks unfair, just as in the case of ביתוס's סריקין.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ruling of חכמים about the סריקין of ביתוס.

steps.title: Challenge: what about the man with only one shirt?
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא challenges אביי from רבי אסי quoting רבי יוחנן: someone who owns only one shirt may launder it on חול המועד. Nobody can see that he has only one shirt, so the 'people will say' worry should forbid it there too.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to your reasoning, what about what רבי אסי said in the name of רבי יוחנן: Anyone who has only one shirt may launder it on חול המועד? There too, people would say, 'All the סריקין are forbidden, yet the סריקין of ביתוס are permitted!'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא attacks אביי's answer by pointing to an accepted rule that allows an exception people cannot see.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן allows a man with one shirt to wash it, even though onlookers cannot tell that he owns only one. If אביי's worry were correct, that rule should not exist. So the 'unseen reason' argument seems too strong.

keyTerms.meaning: And according to your reasoning, a challenge that turns someone's logic against him
The middle days of the festival

steps.confusionAlert: This line uses אביי's own words, but it is not agreeing with him. It repeats his line to show that it would wrongly forbid the one-shirt case too.

phrases.english: And according to your reasoning,
that which Rabbi Asi said
that Rabbi Yoḥanan said:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל מִי שֶׁאֵין לוֹ אֶלָּא חָלוּק אֶחָד
phrases.english: Anyone who has only one shirt
is permitted to launder it on the intermediate days of the festival,
there too, people will say:
All the decorated cakes are forbidden,
but the decorated cakes of Baitos are permitted!

steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's claim that exceptions onlookers cannot see are not allowed.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוחנן allows a man with only one shirt to launder it, even though onlookers cannot see his reason. So אביי's 'people will say' worry would contradict an accepted rule.

steps.title: The belt shows why he is laundering
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the challenge from the one-shirt case: it is not hidden, because his belt proves he has no other shirt.
steps.simpleTranslation: Wasn't it already said about this? מר בר רב אשי said: his belt proves his situation for him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the challenge from step 9. It says the one-shirt man is not a hidden case at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge assumed nobody can see that he owns only one shirt. מר בר רב אשי says they can: while the shirt is being washed, he wears his cloak tied with a belt over bare skin. Since onlookers can tell why he is laundering, the 'people will say' worry does not apply, and אביי's rule stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Wasn't it already said about this? (introduces an earlier answer)
Proves it for him; makes his situation obvious

phrases.english: Wasn't it already said about this:
phrases.notes: The גמרא is answering the one-shirt challenge from step 9.

phrases.english: Mar bar Rav Ashi said:
His belt proves it for him.
phrases.notes: With his only shirt in the wash, he wears his cloak belted shut, so people can see he has no shirt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the קשיא of step 9 against אביי.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Factual distinction: the one-shirt case is visibly obvious, unlike the lost-item case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Nobody can tell the man has only one shirt, so the 'people will say' worry should forbid laundering.
steps.terutzMaskana: His belted cloak shows everyone he has no shirt, so it is permitted. The lost-item case stays forbidden, as אביי said.

steps.title: A craftsman who lost an item before the festival
steps.stepSummary: In רב אשי's version, רבי זירא asks about a craftsman who lost something on ערב הרגל: is his situation obvious enough to allow grooming on חול המועד?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי taught it differently: רבי זירא asked: a craftsman who lost an item on ערב הרגל, what is the law? Since he is a craftsman, is the matter obvious? Or perhaps, since it is not as obvious as those cases in the משנה, he may not?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second version of רבי זירא's question from step 7. Here the person who lost something is a craftsman.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A craftsman works in a public shop. Many customers may have seen him busy searching, so people might know why he could not groom. The question is whether that is public enough, or still less obvious than the clear cases in the משנה, like someone coming from overseas.

keyTerms.meaning: Teaches; gives his version of the passage
Craftsman, a worker with a shop
The matter is evident; people can tell

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new question added to the first one. It is רב אשי's different version of the same question from step 7. In his version the question is only about a craftsman.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi taught it this way:
phrases.notes: This is another version of רבי זירא's question from step 7.

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira asked:
A craftsman who lost an item
on the eve of the festival, what is the law?
Since he is a craftsman,
the matter is evident,
or perhaps, since
the matter is not as evident as those cases,
phrases.notes: 'Those' means the cases listed in the משנה, like someone returning from overseas.

phrases.english: he may not?

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָשֵׁי מַתְנֵי, בָּעֵי רַבִּי זֵירָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different version of the step 7 question, limited to a craftsman.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is a craftsman's being held back public enough to allow grooming on חול המועד?

steps.title: The question stays unresolved
steps.stepSummary: The question about the craftsman is left open: תיקו.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let it stand.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא ends רב אשי's version of the question without an answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version, no answer like אביי's is given. The question of whether a craftsman's situation counts as obvious stays open.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it stand; the question is left unresolved

steps.whatToRemember: An exception for grooming on חול המועד depends on whether people can see why he was held back. אביי forbade the plain lost-item case, the one-shirt man is allowed because his belt shows it, and the craftsman case is left unresolved (תיקו).

phrases.english: Let it stand unresolved.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the question of step 11 without an answer.

steps.title: The משנה does not follow רבי יהודה about overseas travelers
steps.stepSummary: The משנה allows someone returning from overseas to cut his hair, but רבי יהודה in a ברייתא forbids it because he left without permission.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'From a country overseas': our משנה is not like רבי יהודה. A ברייתא teaches that רבי יהודה says: one who comes from overseas may not shave, because he left without permission.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new phrase in the משנה about someone returning from overseas. It points out that רבי יהודה disagrees with the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה treats the returning traveler as held back by forces beyond his control, so he may cut his hair. רבי יהודה says his trip was his own choice, made without permission. So his not grooming before the רגל is his own doing, and he gets no exception.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה does not follow (a certain תנא)
As it was taught (introduces a ברייתא)
He may not shave or cut his hair

phrases.english: "From a country overseas."
phrases.notes: Quoting the משנה, which lets someone back from overseas cut his hair on חול המועד.

phrases.english: Our Mishnah is not like Rabbi Yehuda,
as it was taught: Rabbi Yehuda says:
One who comes from a country overseas
may not shave,
because he left without permission.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins discussion of a new case from the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה allows the overseas traveler to cut his hair. רבי יהודה forbids it because he left without permission.

steps.title: רבא narrows the disagreement to travel for profit
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains the dispute. Leaving for pleasure is forbidden by all, and leaving to make a basic living is permitted by all. They argue only about leaving to make extra profit.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: if he left to roam, all agree it is forbidden. If he left to earn a basic living, all agree it is permitted. They disagree only about leaving for extra profit. One Sage compares it to roaming, and the other compares it to earning a living.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא defines what 'without permission' means and pins down exactly where the משנה and רבי יהודה disagree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Traveling for pleasure is fully his own choice, so nobody gives an exception. Leaving to make a basic living counts as being forced, so everyone allows it. Leaving for extra money is in between: רבי יהודה treats it like a pleasure trip, and the משנה treats it like a trip to make a living.

keyTerms.meaning: To roam or travel for pleasure
For basic living, to support himself

steps.whatToRemember: Both sides agree on the extremes. Leaving for pleasure gets no exception, and leaving to make a basic living gets one. The only dispute is leaving for extra profit: רבי יהודה forbids, and the משנה permits.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that רבי יהודה and the משנה share the same principle: an exception only for someone forced by circumstances. They differ only on how to classify one kind of trip.

phrases.english: Rava said:
If he left to roam, all agree it is forbidden;
if he left to earn a living, all agree it is permitted;
they disagree only about leaving for extra profit.
One Sage compares it to roaming,
phrases.notes: This first Sage is רבי יהודה, who forbids it.

phrases.english: and the other Sage compares it to earning a living.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines the scope of the dispute introduced in step 13.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Leaving for pleasure is forbidden by all, and leaving to make a basic living is permitted by all. Leaving for extra profit is the dispute: רבי יהודה forbids, and the משנה permits.

steps.title: רבי's ruling seems to point to the extra-profit case
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא where רבי says רבי יהודה is right when the person left 'without permission.' Using רבא's categories, that can only mean leaving for extra profit.
steps.simpleTranslation: The גמרא objects: רבי said, 'רבי יהודה's view seems right when the person left without permission, and the חכמים' view seems right when he left with permission.' What does 'without permission' mean? If it means a pleasure trip, you said everyone forbids that! If it means for a basic living, you said everyone permits that! So it must mean for extra profit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts an attack on רבא's explanation from step 14. In this first half, it uses רבא's own categories to pin down what רבי meant by 'without permission.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא said there is no argument about pleasure trips (everyone forbids) or a basic living (everyone permits). So if רבי is choosing a side, it must be in the one disputed case, extra profit. That makes רבי say רבי יהודה is right about extra profit. This is the setup for the contradiction in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: They raised an objection (usually from a ברייתא or משנה)
To wander or travel for pleasure

steps.confusionAlert: 'רבי' alone means רבי יהודה הנשיא, the compiler of the משנה. 'רבי יהודה' is a different תנא, the one who forbids the haircut.

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
Rabbi said:
phrases.notes: This is רבי יהודה הנשיא, not the רבי יהודה who is arguing here.

phrases.english: The words of Rabbi Yehudah seem right
when he left without permission,
and the words of the Sages when he left with permission.
What is 'without permission'?
If you say it means to travel for pleasure,
but you said that all agree it is forbidden!
Rather, it means for a basic living,
but you said that all agree it is permitted!
Rather, it is obvious: for extra profit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests רבא's three-way split against a ברייתא of רבי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Under רבא's categories, 'without permission' can only mean extra profit, so רבי rules like רבי יהודה there. This sets up a clash with the second half.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי: רבי יהודה is right when one left without permission; the חכמים are right when one left with permission.

steps.title: The second half points to the same case, causing a contradiction
steps.stepSummary: 'With permission' must also mean extra profit, so רבי seems to rule both ways on the same case.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now look at the end: 'The חכמים' view seems right when he left with permission.' What does 'with permission' mean? If it means for a basic living, you said everyone permits that! If it means for extra profit, you already said רבי יהודה is right in that case!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the attack by running the same test on the second half of רבי's statement. Both halves end up about extra profit, so they contradict each other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'With permission' cannot mean a basic living, because there is no argument there. So it must mean extra profit. But the first half already gave extra profit to רבי יהודה. רבי cannot side with both opinions in the same case, so it looks like רבא's categories are wrong.

phrases.english: Say the end clause:
The words of the Sages seem right when he left with permission.
What is 'with permission'?
If you say it means for a basic living,
you said that all agree it is permitted!
Rather, it means for extra profit,

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא אָמְרַתְּ נִרְאִין דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בְּהָא!
phrases.english: but you said the words of Rabbi Yehudah seem right in this case!
phrases.notes: This refers to the first half, which we just showed must be about extra profit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the objection begun in step 15 by showing an internal contradiction
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's three categories as applied to רבי's ברייתא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both halves of רבי's statement reduce to the extra-profit case, so רבי would be ruling like both sides in one case.

steps.title: רבי shows where each side admits the other is right
steps.stepSummary: רבי was not deciding the argument. He meant that the חכמים agree with רבי יהודה about pleasure trips, and רבי יהודה agrees with the חכמים about trips for a basic living.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what רבי means: רבי יהודה's view seems right even to the חכמים when the person left without permission, meaning a pleasure trip. The חכמים argue only about extra profit, but about pleasure trips they agree with him. And the חכמים' view seems right even to רבי יהודה when the person left with permission, meaning for a basic living. רבי יהודה argues only about extra profit, but about a basic living he agrees with them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the contradiction by rereading רבי's words. 'Seems right' means 'the other side agrees here,' not 'this is the ruling.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once 'seems right' means 'the other side admits it,' the two halves describe the two cases with no argument: a pleasure trip (forbidden) and a basic living (permitted). The extra-profit case is simply left disputed. This fits רבא exactly, so רבא's explanation stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Agrees / they agree (admits the other side is right)

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהודה and the חכמים argue only about leaving for extra profit. Everyone forbids the haircut after a pleasure trip, and everyone permits it after a trip for a basic living. רבי's statement just spells out these points of agreement.

phrases.english: This is what he is saying:
The words of Rabbi Yehudah seem right to the Rabbis
when he left without permission,
and what is that? To travel for pleasure,
since even the Sages did not disagree with him
except about extra profit,
but about a pleasure trip, they agree with him.
And the words of the Rabbis seem right to Rabbi Yehudah
when he left with permission,
and what is that? For a basic living,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאֲפִילּוּ רַבִּי יְהוּדָה לֹא נֶחְלַק עֲלֵיהֶם
phrases.english: since even Rabbi Yehudah did not disagree with them
except about extra profit,
but about a basic living, he agrees with them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction raised in steps 15-16
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the wording ('seems right' = 'the other side admits')
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי was deciding the argument, so both halves had to be about the disputed extra-profit case.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי was describing the cases where each side agrees with the other, which matches רבא's three categories exactly.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבא's explanation stands: the only dispute is about leaving for extra profit.

steps.title: שמואל: a baby born on the מועד may get a haircut
steps.stepSummary: שמואל rules that a baby born during the מועד may have his hair cut, because the womb kept him from cutting it before.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: A baby born during the מועד may have his hair cut during the מועד, because there is no bigger 'prison' than this.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic starts. שמואל adds another case to the list of people allowed to cut hair on חול המועד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The basic idea in this סוגיא is that someone who could not cut his hair before the holiday may cut it on the מועד, for example a person released from prison. שמואל says a newborn fits this even better, since being in the womb is the ultimate 'prison.'

phrases.english: Shmuel said:
A baby born during the festival
is permitted to have his hair cut during the festival,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאֵין לְךָ בֵּית הָאֲסוּרִין גָּדוֹל מִזֶּה.
phrases.english: for there is no greater prison than this.
phrases.notes: 'This' means his mother's womb, where no one could cut his hair.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new case in the list of people permitted to cut hair on the מועד
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A baby born on the מועד may have his hair cut on the מועד, since the womb prevented it earlier.

steps.title: What שמואל's wording implies: only a baby born on the מועד
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reads שמואל closely: born on the מועד, yes; born before the מועד, no.
steps.simpleTranslation: Born during the מועד, yes. Born before it, no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws a careful inference from שמואל's words. This inference sets up the next discussion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל said 'born during the מועד.' That implies a baby born before the holiday may not get a haircut on the מועד, since there was time to cut his hair before the holiday began.

phrases.english: During the festival, yes;
from before, no.
phrases.notes: He means a baby born before the festival, who could have had his hair cut then.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws an inference from the exact wording of שמואל's ruling
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only a baby born on the מועד is included; a baby born before the holiday is not.

steps.title: רב פנחס quotes a ברייתא linking the festival and mourning
steps.stepSummary: רב פנחס begins a challenge with a ברייתא: everyone allowed to cut his hair on חול המועד may also cut it during his days of mourning.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פנחס challenged from a ברייתא: All the people about whom the חכמים said they may cut their hair on חול המועד may also cut their hair during their days of mourning.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פנחס brings a ברייתא as the opening of a challenge. The גמרא is setting up its next move. The challenge itself is not stated yet.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא ties two separate rules together. The special people allowed to cut on חול המועד (like someone whom circumstances kept from cutting before the festival) are also allowed to cut during אבילות. Because the two lists match, what is true for one should be true for the other.

keyTerms.meaning: raises an objection, usually from a ברייתא or משנה

phrases.english: Rav Pinchas raised an objection:
All those about whom they said
it is permitted to cut hair on the Festival —
it is permitted to cut hair during the days of his mourning.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the close reading of שמואל's ruling about a baby born on the מועד, רב פנחס brings a ברייתא to open a challenge.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling just discussed about haircuts on the מועד. The challenge is completed on the next amud.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: It sets up a source that makes the haircut rules for חול המועד and for mourning match each other.

steps.title: Reading the ברייתא the other way: forbidden on the festival means forbidden in mourning
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא is read in reverse: anyone forbidden to cut his hair on חול המועד is also forbidden to cut it during his days of mourning.
steps.simpleTranslation: This means that one who is forbidden to cut his hair on חול המועד is also forbidden to cut his hair during his days of mourning.
steps.whatsHappening: The challenge reads the ברייתא closely and pulls out the flip side of what it says. This inference is the tool the challenge will use next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא openly states only the 'permitted' side. With the word הָא, the reverse is drawn from it: if the festival is forbidden, mourning is forbidden too. Now the two rules are tied in both directions, and that will be used to challenge the earlier ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: this implies / it follows that (introduces an inference)

steps.confusionAlert: The words 'forbidden on the festival means forbidden in mourning' are not written in the ברייתא. They are a reading of it. The word הָא signals 'from this we learn'.

phrases.english: This implies: one forbidden to cut hair on the Festival —
is forbidden to cut hair during the days of his mourning.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the reverse inference from the ברייתא quoted in step 20.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling being challenged by רב פנחס. The challenge is spelled out on the next amud.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Linking the two rules in both directions means that whoever may not cut on the מועד also may not cut during mourning. This sets up a conflict with the earlier ruling.
